subject.title: [Bug]: Concurrent allow-always approvals silently lose allowlist entries (last-write-wins race in exec-approvals.json)

question: Should maintainers adopt or replace the shared guarded-write fix path for exec approval stale writes, or sponsor a narrower allow-always-only fix for this issue?
rationale: The bug affects approval persistence and security state, and there are overlapping open and closed PRs with unresolved proof/review blockers, so automation should not start another fix branch without maintainer direction.

options.title: Adopt or replace the shared guarded-write fix
options.body: Use the broader guarded-write/CAS direction from the existing fix attempt, but refresh it on current main and close the review/proof gaps before merge.

options.title: Sponsor a narrow allow-always fix
options.body: Limit the repair to concurrent `allow-always` persistence if maintainers want to defer the broader execution metadata security fix.

options.title: Wait for the security PR track
options.body: Keep this issue open and let the node stale-writeback security fix decide the shared persistence primitive first.

recommendation.title: Adopt or replace the shared guarded-write fix
recommendation.body: Use the broader guarded-write/CAS direction from the existing fix attempt, but refresh it on current main and close the review/proof gaps before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: They authored recent merged exec approval durability work and the open maintainer gateway freshness guard adjacent to the same persistence boundary.
